chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Safwan from Rifa'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about a man who divorced his wife until she became irrevocably divorced from him and her waiting period ended, then she married another husband, so he divorced her as well, then her first husband married her again. Does that demolish the first divorce? He said: Yes.
ai.seo_question: Does a second marriage and subsequent divorce nullify the first irrevocable divorce in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of 'Tahliyah' (or 'Tasbiyah'), where a third divorce is required to make the initial divorce irrevocable. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that if the wife marries another man and he divorces her, the first husband's initial divorce is 'demolished' (haddama), allowing her to return to him under the same original marriage contract without a new mahr or contract. This ruling is pivotal in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between revocable (raj'i) and irrevocable (ba'in) divorces, ensuring the first husband can remarry his ex-wife without the restrictions of a new marriage ceremony.
